For `r SiteSummary$scope$nVs30` site conditions between $V_{S30}=`r .fmt(min(SiteSummary$siteConditions), 0)`$ and `r .fmt(max(SiteSummary$siteConditions), 0)` m/s and `r SiteSummary$scope$nTR` return periods between `r .fmti(min(SiteSummary$returnPeriods))` and `r .fmti(max(SiteSummary$returnPeriods))` years, the mean envelope demand spans PGA from `r .fmt(SiteSummary$pga[TR == min(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), minimum])` to `r .fmt(SiteSummary$pga[TR == min(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), maximum])` g for $T_R=`r .fmti(min(SiteSummary$returnPeriods))`$ years and from `r .fmt(SiteSummary$pga[TR == max(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), minimum])` to `r .fmt(SiteSummary$pga[TR == max(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), maximum])` g for $T_R=`r .fmti(max(SiteSummary$returnPeriods))`$ years. The UHS maxima of that same envelope range from `r .fmt(SiteSummary$peak[TR == min(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), minimum])` to `r .fmt(SiteSummary$peak[TR == min(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), maximum])` g at the shortest of those return periods and from `r .fmt(SiteSummary$peak[TR == max(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), minimum])` to `r .fmt(SiteSummary$peak[TR == max(SiteSummary$returnPeriods), maximum])` g at the longest; each interval is the spread across the site conditions at a fixed return period. These values come from the envelope of two branches: the GMPE-based branch, which evaluates the ground-motion logic tree directly at the target $V_{S30}$, and the amplification-based branch, which applies the nonlinear amplification factor to the mean UHS at the reference condition $V_{\mathrm{ref}}=760$ m/s.
